name: PR replay pilot: Claude Code with its own memory, plus Snout trimming, plus Snout memory
protocol: docs/benchmark-protocol.md#memory-study (the memory study's grading and validity rules), with the replay changes below
question: On real issues from projects we did not write, each started from the commit before its fix with the project's real history up to that commit, does Snout's trimming, and Snout's trimming plus memory, lower cost per solved task against Claude Code with its own memory, without solving fewer?

arms.plain: Claude Code with its own memory (auto memory, on by default); no Snout
arms.trim: plain plus Snout's read gate and output trimming; Snout memory off
arms.search: trim plus Snout memory as it ships: session records from earlier tasks in the chain, the project's history imported up to the base (snout import, six months back from the base's date, git only), the session-start hint, the memory skill (as the plugin ships it; added 2026-11-10 before any paid session, docs/benchmark-protocol.md), and memory search and fetch as MCP tools; the agent decides whether to search

replay.workspace: one folder per chain (arm and repeat), so Claude Code's own memory and Snout's records carry from task to task as in a developer's clone
replay.history: each task fetches only its base and the base's ancestors from the local clone, in merge order; before every session the fix's commit must be absent and every ref must reach only the base's ancestors, or the run stops
replay.ownMemory: Claude Code's memory folder for the chain's workspace is emptied when the chain opens and measured after every session; if Claude Code writes none in headless runs, plain is reported as Claude Code without memory in practice
replay.grading: the fix PR's own tests over the agent's work, against the base commit (a session that commits is graded on its work)

pilot.purpose: feasibility and size, not a claim: does the replay run cleanly with a real agent, do agents use either memory, and how much do arms vary, to size the full run
pilot.valid: every chain valid (no leak, no network use, no Snout side call, hooks seen where Snout runs), and every session graded
pilot.proceedToFullRun: valid, and search solves no fewer than trim minus one task on the pilot; otherwise diagnose the memory path before any further paid run
pilot.reported: solved, cost and cost per solved task per arm; search vs trim and search vs plain (point estimates only, fewer than 10 tasks per repository); memory use (searched, opened, acted on); wrong recalls (acted on a record and failed a task trim solved); Claude Code's own memory files per session; tokens Snout kept out

fullRun.tasks: the held-out tasks above plus a third repository not used in any development (to be chosen and frozen before the full run)
fullRun.primary: cost per solved task, search vs plain, paired by task, 95% bootstrap interval
fullRun.secondary: search vs trim (does memory add to trimming), solved-fraction difference with a one-sided 95% lower bound against a 10-point margin, wrong recalls
fullRun.claim: a savings claim only if the interval lies below 1 and the solved-fraction lower bound stays within the margin

caveats: vite's commit history was a development set for the history search thresholds on 2026-11-09 (bench/import-asof/vite); these are vite issue tasks, not those commits, and the full run adds a repository never used in development
the pilot's chains are five tasks long, so earlier-session records are few; imported history is the main memory source here
